title: Buchary1999 thesis, Table3.1 PDF58–59/printed49–50 and habitat/size prose PDF55/46
supports: Actual representative taxonomy; habitat first, then average or maximum length<40/40–60/>60cm. Family-level summary, not exhaustive modern membership. Infauna cutoff visually<=1.0mm, accepted stored description retained.

title: Buchary1999 Table3.9 PDF80/printed71 and catch-assumption prose PDF69–76
supports: Complete printed Harvest, including genuine zeros. Juvenile shrimp and large-demersal juvenile catches are author assumptions; LBS is10×SAF assumed bycatch. Numerical model-catch fractions are Medium composition proxies, not observed stage-mass fractions.

title: Sea Around Us LME38 v50.1 original catch ZIP
supports: 181 exact reported labels and original country/sector/catch type/reporting/gear/end-use/year fields. Generic key100039/100139/100239/100339 bony residual scope excludes dedicated cartilage. Provider30/90cm tags differ from source40/60cm rules.

title: LME_038 workbook, protected Classic PPR coefficients and annual outputs
supports: Reference2019 landings, classic taxon TL/coefficient and valid bounds preserved. Simple-chain PPR equals wet coefficient×catch/9 once.39 coefficient-missing taxa have genuine zero2019 catch and zero annual contribution.

title: Actual historical identified-catch donor and raw-strata review
supports: All eligible non-unidentified direct/stage donors in candidate guilds,1950–2019 total catch, no same-family restriction.16 prior fractions independently reproduced; proxy composition/basis mismatch remains Low.

title: Complete candidate and allocation ledger
supports: Every181 label, eligible/excluded groups, source Harvest/biomass, genuine-zero candidates, membership/allocation confidence and exact weights. Zero numerical weights remain in ledger.

title: Fresh GE/TE/With Egestion full source matrices
supports: 29 loaded groups including synthetic import;29×4source entries each;348 total finite/nonnegative. Saved scoped coefficients match. TE Marine mammals near-zero warning retained.

title: Java Sea source bounds and LME overlay
supports: Approximate source prose bounds, two eastern scenarios, 1:50 million coast clipping. A≈19–22%,B≈99–100%; no explicit source polygon; no catch/PPR multiplier.

title: FAO 1974 species sheets, historical Pentapodidae
supports: PDF 2–4: Pentapodus, Gnathodentex, Monotaxis and Gymnocranius are included; Scolopsis is absent. Supports historical Pentapodus source 8 bridge, not a whole-modern-family synonym or a Scolopsis SAF assignment.

title: FAO 1974 species sheets, historical Nemipteridae
supports: PDF 2–3: Nemipterus, Parascolopsis and Scolopsis are separate from Pentapodidae. Supports source Small demersals connection; representative regional family contents remain incomplete.

title: FAO 1990 catalogue, Nemipteridae introduction
supports: PDF 4–6: modern Nemipteridae includes Nemipterus/Scolopsis and Pentapodus; benthic/reef habitats vary. Supports coarse family 21/8 boundary and partial Scolopsis fit without proving living-structure dependence or actual catch proportions.

title: FAO 1993 groupers catalogue, Cephalopholis overview
supports: Genus/habitat context for the historical Serranidae source family. Genus ecology is representative; the species-specific C.boenak account carries the relevant size/habitat evidence.

title: FAO 1993 groupers catalogue, Cephalopholis boenak
supports: PDF 6/printed 38: maximum TL 26 cm,4–30 m silty dead reefs in protected waters, trawled to 64 m. Supports source<40 cm Small demersals. Dead-reef occurrence alone does not prove source SAF living-structure dependence.

title: FAO Western Central Pacific guide, Pomadasys argenteus
supports: PDF 7/printed 2983: maximum about 60 cm, common 40 cm; coastal bays and estuaries. Positively supports source 40–60 cm Medium demersals; source average-or-maximum convention and unobserved landed size leave a Small alternative uncertain.

title: FAO Western Central Pacific guide, Megalops cyprinoides
supports: Printed 1622: maximum TL 55 cm, common 30 cm; coastal lagoons/estuaries and open-water swimming. Supports Misc. pelagics analogy and contradicts automatic placement from provider>=90 cm tag. Lineage and estuarine migration differ.

title: FAO Pakistan guide, Platycephalidae
supports: Printed 30: bottom-associated flathead species have maxima 25,50 and 100 cm. Supports family size diversity and explicit 21/22/23/26 demersal analogues; does not observe Java Sea size or catch composition.

title: FAO Maldives account, Plotosus lineatus
supports: Species maximum 32 cm supports a small constituent; reef/coastal occurrence. A species account cannot establish genus/family-wide small-only membership or caught-stage proportions.

title: FAO Western Central Pacific guide, Plotosidae
supports: Printed 1883: P.lineatus maximum about 30 cm; P.canius common<=80 cm. Historical maximum 150 cm is questioned and is not measured Java Sea composition. Supports small-through-large catfish analogues, with Very low membership.

title: FAO 1993 catalogue, historical scombroid scope
supports: Historical scombroid fisheries concept includes tunas, bonitos, mackerels, billfish and barracudas. Supports provider-category interpretation and actual source scombrid/barracuda connections; modern order identity and local species composition differ.
